triggerReason: A safely staged intervention still had no independent delayed evaluation, invalidatable organizational memory, context-checked reuse, or governed path from evidence to the next improvement proposal.
action: Added an independent deterministic Outcome Evaluator with three horizons and frozen comparisons, late-evidence revision and incident reopening, a lineage-preserving Lesson Registry, invalidation-aware response playbooks, governed learning proposals, durable memory/PostgreSQL services and APIs, and a bilingual Learning Observatory.
outcome: NEXUS-7 can now distinguish short-term movement from sustained synthetic benefit, retain failure and uncertainty, revise conclusions when late harm arrives, prevent harmful or invalid memory from becoming a recommendation, and route learning back through the existing controlled release chain.
evidence: The evaluator is explicitly independent from proposing Agents and records deterministic repeated fingerprints
Every outcome evaluates 15-, 60-, and 180-tick windows against frozen, historical, and same-seed seasonal comparisons
Beneficial, harmful, neutral, and inconclusive verdicts are represented in the acceptance corpus
Late synthetic harm creates a new outcome revision, invalidates superseded lessons and playbooks, and reopens the city incident
Success, failure, rollback, and inconclusive lessons remain in the registry with complete outcome provenance
Only validated success lessons are positive-retrieval eligible
Playbook reuse rechecks lesson, context, drift, trust, capability, budget, experiment, and human approval gates
Generated policy, prompt, scenario, and test requests cannot bypass controlled iteration
Memory and PostgreSQL round-trip outcomes, lessons, playbooks, proposals, and invalidation lineage
Learning Observatory exposes prediction error, contradictions, human correction, provenance, and the synthetic boundary in English and Chinese
